Our revisions retain a thirty-day closing target, subject to regulatory approvals and customary objective closing protections. edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. Buyer shall purchase the Shares for a fixed aggregate purchase price of USD [amount to be agreed before execution] (the Purchase Price), payable entirely in immediately available funds at Closing to an account designated by Seller. There shall be no escrow, holdback or post-Closing purchase-price adjustment.
edits.name: Fixed cash consideration

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after signing, subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals, absence of any legal prohibition, and delivery of customary closing deliverables, including instruments transferring good title to the Shares free of liens. Buyer's obligation to close is also subject to Seller's fundamental representations being true in all respects, its other representations being true in all material respects, and Seller having performed its pre-Closing covenants in all material respects; any representation already qualified by materiality shall be tested as written without an additional materiality qualification. Seller's obligation to close is subject to Buyer's material performance and payment of the Purchase Price. There shall be no financing contingency or further diligence condition. Each party shall use reasonable best efforts to obtain required approvals and satisfy the conditions within its control. If regulatory approvals remain outstanding on day thirty, Closing shall occur within five business days after satisfaction or waiver of the remaining conditions. Either party may terminate if Closing has not occurred by day ninety, unless its breach caused the failure to close.
edits.name: Closing mechanics and objective protections

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Seller represents at signing and Closing that: (a) Seller and the Company are duly organized and validly existing; (b) Seller has authority to execute and perform this Agreement, which constitutes its binding obligation; (c) Seller owns the Shares free of liens and may transfer good title, and the disclosed capitalization of the Company is complete and accurate; (d) the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results in accordance with the accounting principles consistently applied and identified in those statements; (e) the Company has no material liabilities other than those reflected or reserved in those statements, specifically disclosed in the disclosure schedules, or incurred in the ordinary course since the latest balance-sheet date; (f) the Company has filed all material required tax returns and paid all material taxes due; (g) the Company complies in all material respects with applicable laws and holds all material permits required for its business; (h) no material litigation is pending or, to Seller's Knowledge, threatened against the Company; (i) the Company is not in material default under any material contract and, to Seller's Knowledge, no counterparty is in material default; and (j) the Company owns or has valid rights to use the material assets and intellectual property used in its business. Exceptions must be fairly disclosed in schedules delivered at signing with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; disclosure against one representation qualifies another only where its relevance is reasonably apparent. Seller's Knowledge means the actual knowledge of Seller's and the Company's chief executive and chief financial officers after reasonable inquiry of personnel responsible for the relevant subject. Paragraphs (a) through (c) are the fundamental representations.
edits.name: Enumerated Seller representations

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Seller shall indemnify Buyer and the Company against actual losses arising from breaches of Seller's representations or covenants and taxes attributable to pre-Closing periods, without double recovery and net of insurance proceeds actually recovered, less reasonable recovery costs. General representations survive for eighteen months after Closing. Claims for their breach are subject to a deductible basket of 0.5% of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap of 15% of the Purchase Price. Fundamental representations survive for six years after Closing; tax representations and pre-Closing tax indemnification survive until sixty days after the applicable limitation period expires. Covenants survive according to their terms or, if no period is specified, until the applicable limitation period expires. The basket and general cap do not apply to fundamental representations, tax claims or covenant breaches, but Seller's aggregate liability under this Section shall not exceed the Purchase Price, except for proven actual fraud by Seller. A claim notified in reasonable detail before the applicable survival period expires survives until finally resolved. Buyer shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate recoverable losses. Seller may control the defense of a third-party claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to Buyer if Seller acknowledges coverage and the claim seeks only monetary relief; no settlement may impose an admission, nonmonetary obligation or unreleased liability on Buyer or the Company without Buyer's consent. Following Closing, this Section is Buyer's exclusive monetary remedy for matters arising under this Agreement, except for proven actual fraud by Seller; specific performance and other equitable relief remain available.
edits.name: Balanced indemnity counterproposal

To resolve the remaining risk allocation, Seller proposes twelve-month general survival, a 1% deductible basket and a 10% general cap, with pre-Closing covenant breaches subject to that basket and cap; the proposed separate treatment of fundamental representations, taxes, actual fraud and equitable enforcement is otherwise acceptable.
